executive_summary: This is the second round on 2026-10-29. It reviews the re-freeze after the REVISE of b6045fa6006e (commit 1d191f9). The new candidate bytes hash to e1a179d37974..., which matches candidate.sha256. The bytes equal the shared canonical form, and canonical(data/current.json) gives the same hash. npm run check passes with 0 structural flags, and the working tree has no frontend or script changes. The diff from 73e7246 touches only boc-h7, boc-h8, boc-d4, fed-h11, fed-h12, fed-d7, total_score.boc and notes. Pricing, calendar and the other drivers are byte-identical to the round-1 bytes, which I verified against primaries and the live Kalshi/Polymarket books. Both round-1 majors are fixed and verified against the new bytes (the validator counts major findings regardless of disposition, so they are recorded here and in review.md rather than as findings). (1) boc-h7.market_validation now covers the whole decision window and calls it 'Mixed'. I re-checked it against the Kalshi 26DEC-H25 trade tape: 09:45:29 @0.46, 09:48:45 @0.35, 09:57:11 @0.33, 10:31-10:59 @0.39-0.42, last 19:07:35Z @0.37. The Bloomberg ~60% figure is now labelled secondary and linked. theglobeandmail.com/business/article-bank-of-canada-raises-interest-rate-october-2026/ (HTTP 200) reads 'a roughly 60-per-cent chance of another hike at the bank's next meeting in December', according to Bloomberg data. (2) boc-h7.data.forecast now attributes the ~96% to CORRA OIS and gives Polymarket at 85.3%, matching git 2516384^. Surprise is set to 0, so the weight is 2+1+0=3 and BoC rescores to 3+2-3=+2 hold, against Kalshi 62.1% hold. The Fed stays at +6 lean hike against 75.6% hike. Round-1 minors: fed-h12 now carries the Q3 price block (2.1% / 2.5% SAAR), fed-h11 and fed-h12 share one combined 08:30 attribution (0.78 -> 0.74, net -4c, matching the hourly candles), and fed-d7 drops the 'main reason' claim. Those three are fixed. Three remain minor and non-blocking: fed-d7's quote is still not verbatim, boc-h8's title still uses opening-statement wording, and boc-h7's stamps are loose. All are noted for the next cycle. The board binds to this sha only.

findings.issue: Partly fixed. The 'main reason December is priced near 75%' claim is gone from the reason. The summary still quotes 'going the right way' for inflation compensation and expectations. Warsh said compensation is 'going in the right way' and expectations 'have gone the right way'. The exact phrase 'going the right way' appears only in a reporter's question.
findings.evidence: https://www.federalreserve.gov/mediacenter/files/FOMCpresconf20261028.pdf (pdftotext): Warsh, 'inflation compensation is going in the right way ... They've gone the right way too'; Capurro (Bloomberg), 'you're saying inflation expectations are going the right way'.

findings.issue: Partly fixed. boc-h8's summary and reason now quote the linked press release ('somewhat stronger', 'stronger than expected in the July Report'). The title still says 'slack absorbed by 2028', which appears only in the opening statement. The press release instead says indicators 'continue to point to some excess supply'.
findings.evidence: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/opening-statement-2026-10-28/: 'This absorbs the remaining slack in the economy'. https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/fad-press-release-2026-10-28/: 'A broad set of indicators continue to point to some excess supply in the economy.'

findings.issue: The stamps are loose. '(BlueGamma, 09:13 ET)' is the freeze time of the morning snapshot, not the BlueGamma reading. The OIS page was stamped 08:27:48 ET. Separately, '-9c net' is measured from the first post-release trade (0.46). The pre-release book was 0.48/0.49, so the net move is closer to -11c. Neither affects the weight or the band.
